findings.evidence: The View details button at line 73 appears before the date-of-birth fieldset that starts at line 74. The form's structure places a non-submit button in the middle of the fields rather than after them.
findings.fix: Move the View details button to after the form's submit button, or ensure it sits only at the form's end alongside the primary action.
findings.violation: A secondary action (View details) is placed above the form's fields, specifically before the date-of-birth fieldset, which violates the principle that all actions should sit at or after the fields end in line with them.

findings.evidence: <select id="dob-day-select" autocomplete="bday-day" required=""> <select id="dob-month-select" autocomplete="bday-month" required=""> <select id="dob-year-select" autocomplete="bday-year" required="">
findings.fix: Use three short text fields for day, month and year, with the numeric input mode.
findings.violation: A date the person knows by heart is picked from three drop-downs, the year from 60 options.

findings.evidence: Both fields have autocomplete='name' and request a person's name. The form also asks for email, password, street address, phone, postal code, shipping speed, and organization - core elements for account creation - making the duplicate name field redundant.
findings.fix: Remove the 'Your name' field and use only the 'Full name' field to capture the person's name.
findings.violation: The form asks for 'Your name' (#legalname-input) in addition to 'Full name' (#name-input), requesting the same information twice. This adds unnecessary work for completing account creation.

findings.evidence: <input id="postal-input" name="postal_code" type="text" autocomplete="postal-code" required="" size="3"> (size=3)
findings.fix: Size the field to show at least 5 characters.
findings.violation: This postal code field shows 3 characters, too few to show a typical value whole while it is typed and checked.

findings.fix: Loosen the pattern to accept every valid way of writing the value, and normalise it after submission.
findings.violation: The pattern on this phone field rejects valid values such as +44 20 7946 0958; 020 7946 0958.

findings.evidence: The form's task is account creation (per the heading 'Create your account' and submit label 'Create account'). Contact time preference is not required to create the account and could be asked in a profile setup flow afterwards.
findings.fix: Remove this field from the account creation form and ask for it after the account is created, such as in an onboarding or preferences flow.
findings.violation: The form asks for 'Preferred contact time' before account creation is complete. This preference could be collected after the account is created, and requiring it now is unnecessary friction.

findings.evidence: font-size: 13px declared by its inline style
findings.fix: Set the field's font size to at least 16 pixels.
findings.violation: The text in this field is 13 pixels, below the 16 pixels at which a phone stops zooming the page on focus.
This web address field is type text, so a phone does not show the keyboard built for it.

findings.evidence: The contacttime-label carries style='display:inline-block;float:left;width:140px', which positions it to the left. Other fields use simple label-input pairs in divs with no positioning, implying vertical stacking.
findings.fix: Either position all labels above their fields consistently, or position all labels beside their fields. If stacking is preferred, remove the float and width styles from the contacttime-label.
findings.violation: The label for 'Preferred contact time' is positioned to the left of its field via float:left and fixed width (140px), placing it beside the field. The form's other labels appear to stack above their fields, creating an inconsistent layout.
